title: Late Payment Charge on an Electric Service Agreement Bill — Posting Reference
content:
**Rule.** A late payment charge is posted on the most recent bill of the agreement once that bill's grace period has ended with part of the bill unpaid and no late payment charge has yet been posted for that bill.

This reference covers that charge on an Electric Service Agreement of Lakeshore Power & Light Company. The charge belongs to the bill: it is one charge, tied to the bill on which it is assessed, and it raises the balance the customer owes on the agreement. The most recent bill is the agreement's bill with the latest bill date.

## The rule in its parts

| Element | What the rule requires |
|---|---|
| Bill concerned | The most recent bill of the agreement |
| Timing | The bill's grace period has ended |
| Payment position | Part of the bill is unpaid |
| Charges already on the bill | No late payment charge has yet been posted for that bill |
| Result | One late payment charge, assessed on that bill |

## Posting tool

The charge is booked with `post_late_payment_charge_a575fa01`, an agent-side tool: the agent unlocks it and then calls it. It books the charge as a new late payment charge dated the day it is called, tied to the bill it was assessed on, and the agreement's balance owed rises by the charged amount; the customer sees the charge on the account at once and on the next bill. One call books exactly one charge for that bill.

### Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `service_account_id` | The service account number of the Electric Service Agreement being charged, as returned by the service agreement lookup | Identifier |
| `bill_id` | The reference number of the bill the late payment charge is assessed on, as returned by the bill lookup for that agreement | Identifier |
| `amount` | The late payment charge in USD | Positive number with 2 decimal places (cents); a value with more decimals is rounded half-up to the cent when it is booked |

### Return

On success the tool returns a confirmation sentence stating the new charge reference number (an opaque identifier beginning "lpc_"), the bill reference number it was assessed on, the booked amount in USD with 2 decimal places, the posting date (YYYY-MM-DD) and the agreement's new balance owed in USD with 2 decimal places. Receiving that sentence means the charge is posted.
